title: Detection of activation-induced cytidine deaminase in gastric epithelial cells infected with cag pathogenicity island-positive Helicobacter pylori
protocol: To 500 ml H₂O, add 22 grams Columbia Blood Agar Base.
Autoclave at 121°C for 20 minutes.
Place the autoclaved media in a 56°C water bath until temperature is achieved.
Pour 35 ml of sterile horse blood into a sterile 50 ml conical tube.
Remove the media from the water bath and quickly add the horse blood, avoiding bubbles.
Add antibiotics to the media: amphotericin B (2.5 mg/l), trimethoprim (5 mg/l), polymyxin B (1250 IU/l), vancomycin (10 mg/l).
Pour the prepared media into Petri dishes.
Let the plates stand until they cool and solidify.
While still moist, place each plate in a plastic sleeve and seal it until needed.
To 500 ml H₂O, add 21.5 grams Brucella Broth.
Autoclave at 121°C for 20 minutes.
Shortly before use, add FBS to 10% and antibiotics as described for the solid media preparation.
Place a drop of liquid culture in the center of each plate or lift a loopful from a 2-4 day old plate with growth.
Spread inoculum across the entire width of the plate using a loop, turning the plate 90° and repeating.
Cover plates and place them in a GasPack jar upside-down.
Add water to the CampyPack Plus envelope according to manufacturer's instructions and quickly place it in the GasPack jar.
Seal the top of the jar well.
Place the sealed jar at 37°C for 2-4 days.
Place 1 ml of sterile broth in the center of a plate with 2-3 days growth of _H. pylori_.
Lift bacteria from the plate by continuous scraping with a sterile glass spreader.
Tip the plate at a shallow angle and gently work all liquid to the lower edge.
Remove 1 ml of bacterial suspension with a pipetman and place in a sterile tube.
Place a 10 μl aliquot on a microscope slide.
Examine the slide at 400X magnification to determine viability and check for contamination.
Inoculate 50 ml of complete media in a sterile tissue culture flask with 1/8 plates worth of bacteria (125 μl).
Keep the cap loose to allow gas exchange during growth.
Grow stationary cultures at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for 24 hours.
Harvest bacteria from plates and transfer to complete liquid media.
Ensure O.D. is less than 0.05 at 450 nm with a spectrophotometer.
Plate out some liquid culture (e.g., 10 μl) on the plates and grow at 37°C.
Every hour, remove an aliquot (e.g., 10 μl).
Read the O.D. at 450 nm.
Record the O.D. and plate some liquid culture on the plates until O.D. begins to increase.
When O.D. begins to increase, test every 30 minutes.
Use at least two plates at each time point.
Dilute samples in different ratios (e.g., 1:10, 1:100, 1:1000, etc.).
Repeat until O.D.450 approaches 0.5.
Grow bacteria for 3-4 days and count the colonies, back-calculating for dilution and volume to determine cfu per ml.
Plot O.D. 450 vs cfu / ml on a graph to generate a growth curve.
Determine the cfu / ml at 0.1 O.D.
Grow AGS human gastric epithelial cells in Ham’s F12 modified medium supplemented with 10% FBS without antibiotics.
Plate AGS cells on 6-well plates and incubate at 37°C with 5% CO₂ overnight.
Determine bacterial density by optical density at 450 nm using a previously established growth curve.
Incubate H. pylori / AGS co-cultures at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for the indicated period.
Confirm that more than 80% of the AGS cells acquire the hummingbird phenotype, which represents cag PAI-positive H. pylori infection.
Extract total RNA from cultured cells 24 h after infection with bacteria using Sepasol-RNA Super-I reagent according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Dissolve RNA into RNase-free water and store at -80°C.
Perform reverse transcription using the Superscript III first strand synthesis system.
Perform polymerase chain reaction amplification using ExTaq polymerase on a GeneAmp PCR System 9700.
Incubate at 94 °C for 1 min., then at 55 °C for 1 min., and finally at 72 °C for 1 min. Repeat this cycle 45 times.
Use non-template controls as negative controls for each amplification.
Use templates derived from AID-overexpressing BL2 cells as positive controls.
Quantify the total β-actin gene transcripts in each sample as an internal control to standardize results.
Perform quantification of human AID gene expression by quantitative real-time RT-PCR using a Real Time PCR System 7300 and TaqMan Universal PCR Master Mix according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Incubate at 50 °C for 2 min., then at 95 °C for 10 min., followed by 45 cycles of 95 °C for 15 sec. and 60 °C for 1 min.
Generate standard curves for AID using a 10-fold serial dilution series of 5 independent transcripts derived from BL2-lymphoma cells highly expressing AID.
Normalize target cDNAs to the endogenous mRNA levels of the housekeeping reference gene 18S ribosomal RNA (18S rRNA).
Collect cells 24 h after infection of bacteria from 6-well plates on ice using a cell scraper.
Wash cells with ice-cold PBS once.
Obtain total cell lysates by lysing the cells in RIPA lysis buffer containing Complete Mini protease inhibitor cocktail tablets.
Store at -80°C.
Determine protein concentration with Protein Assay Dye Reagent Concentrate.
Add SDS sample buffer with β-ME to the sample proteins to achieve the same concentration.
Boil samples at 100 °C for 5 min.
Resolve protein samples on 1.5 mm-thick 12.5% SDS-PAGE gels and run at 100 V for 1 h with Mini-PROTEAN 3 Cell according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Pre-equilibrate SDS-PAGE gels in transfer buffer prior to electrophoretic transfer.
Electrophoretically transfer proteins from gels to polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) membranes (pore size; 0.2 μm) at 20 mA for 17.5-20 h.
Pre-wet PVDF membranes in 100% methanol and then rinse in transfer buffer before electrophoretic transfer.
Block with blocking buffer at room temperature for 1 hour.
Incubate with polyclonal antibodies against human AID in PBST supplemented with 10% blocking buffer at 4°C overnight.
Wash membranes with PBST three times.
Incubate with secondary antibody in PBST supplemented with 10% blocking buffer at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Wash membranes with PBST three times.
Wash membranes with PBS once.
Perform ECL. Add Immobilon Western Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate on PVDF membranes.
Expose on the film and develop.
After detection of AID protein, wash PVDF membranes with water.
Block with blocking buffer at room temperature for 1 hour.
Incubate cells with primary polyclonal α-tubulin-specific antibody at 4°C overnight.
Wash membranes with PBST three times.
Incubate with secondary antibody in PBST supplemented with 10% blocking buffer at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Wash membranes with PBST three times.
Wash membranes with PBS once.
Perform ECL. Add Immobilon Western Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate on PVDF membranes.
Expose on the film and develop.
Grow AGS cells on Lab-Tek Chamber Slide System glass slides.
24 hours after infection with H. pylori, wash cells with PBS and fix in 10% formalin/PBS solution at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Wash cells with PBS.
Permeabilize with 0.1% Triton X-100/PBS solution at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Wash cells with PBS.
Quench endogenous peroxidase activity with 0.3% H2O2/methanol at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Wash cells with PBS.
Block with 1% BSA/PBS solution.
Incubate cells with primary polyclonal AID-specific antibody at 4°C overnight.
Wash cells with PBS.
Incubate cells with biotinylated secondary antibody at room temperature for 30 min.
Wash cells with PBS.
Add ABC reagent, avidin/biotinylated enzyme complex.
Wash cells with PBS.
Incubate cells with DAB Substrate until the desired stain intensity develops.
Rinse cells with water to stop development by DAB substrate.
Mount cells in Mount-Quick.
